ct_killingworth.blurb: Killingworth is a bouldering area in Connecticut, made up of pockets of boulders in the country around Chatfield Hollow, off Route 80. Every climb is a boulder problem, with grades from V0 through V10 and the heaviest concentration between V3 and V5. Roofs, caves and cracks feature among the problems. The bedrock in Chatfield Hollow is gneiss, and the hollow also holds rockfall caves and rounded glacial boulders left behind by the ice. Chatfield Weather Caves, Broken Bridge and Fat Man's Squeeze hold the most climbs.

ok_dog_run_hollow_area.blurb: Dog Run Hollow is a bouldering-focused part of the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge in Oklahoma. Nearly all of the climbs are boulder problems, with a few trad lines, and the grades run from V0 to V10 with most falling between V1 and V4. At Slab Lands, which holds the most climbs here, the boulders range from very big, proud blocks to smaller, less intimidating lines, with most problems from V0 to V5. Hilton's Hill West adds more. Climbing across the refuge is on granite, with spring and fall the most popular seasons; summer climbers look for shade and winter climbers for sun.

sd_chopping_block.blurb: Chopping Block is a climbing area among the Needles of Rushmore in South Dakota. It holds sport routes, trad lines and boulder problems, with sport the largest share. Roped grades run from easy to 5.13 and cluster around 5.10, and the boulders go from V1 up to V10. The formations are long one-pitch blocks rather than a forest of spires, giving a concentration of hard routes with some good moderates mixed in. Across the Rushmore climbing area the rock is pegmatite granite, and there is climbing on every aspect from spring to fall. Veiny holds the most climbs, followed by Meat Counter and Three Amigos Boulder.

ut_box_canyon.blurb: Box Canyon is a narrow canyon at the mouth of Maple Canyon in central Utah, at about 6,600 feet. Sport climbing dominates, and the grades lean hard: most of the bolted routes are 5.12 or harder, with a handful of moderates at EFS Wall. The canyon is cool and shady almost all day because it is so narrow and runs north to south. Maple Canyon's rock is conglomerate, with rounded cobbles set into the walls and a wide range of holds. Jehovah Wall, EFS Wall and Ammo Dump Wall hold the most climbs.

ut_ogden_canyon.blurb: Ogden Canyon runs east from Ogden into the Wasatch Range, and most of its routes are within the first mile up the canyon. Trad leads, with a good share of sport and a few boulder problems and aid lines. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.13 and mostly sit between 5.6 and 5.11. The climbs are short, usually 30 to 85 feet, on slabby rock just short of vertical. At Utah Wall the lines are clean quartzite and classic cracks, best from late spring through fall and shaded when it is hot. The 5.8 Wall is best in spring and fall. Utah Wall, The Ice Wall and The Diamond hold the most climbs.
